title: Deadly 7.1-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Southern Japan, Killing at Least 13 With Dozens Still Missing
excerpt: A powerful quake in Kumamoto prefecture triggered a massive explosion at the region's largest shopping mall, collapsed bridges and buildings, and forced the evacuation of over 10,000 people.
body:
• A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Japan's Kumamoto prefecture on Kyushu island on Tuesday, killing at least 13 people with 19 still missing as of Wednesday morning.
  • An explosion at the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto — the prefecture's largest shopping center — tore away one side of the building, killing two women in their twenties and leaving 10 workers unaccounted for.
  • More than 10,000 people have been evacuated to over 500 shelters, with 36,000 homes without power and critical infrastructure including bridges and highways severely damaged.
  • Japan's Meteorological Agency warned of possible strong aftershocks for the next week and the risk of landslides in the mountainous region.

The Quake and Its Aftermath

The earthquake struck at mid-afternoon local time on Tuesday, centered in Kumamoto prefecture on Japan's southwestern island of Kyushu. The 7.1-magnitude tremor toppled buildings, ruptured roads, sparked fires, and knocked out power to tens of thousands of homes.

https://x.com/MyLordBebo/status/2082056675163505011

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said authorities were still assessing the full extent of the damage. "We have already been informed that people have been injured. Power outages and fires have occurred in some areas, and there has also been damage to roads and bridges and the collapse of buildings," Takaichi said, urging residents to evacuate to safe locations.

Around 300,000 people were instructed to move to evacuation centers, and hundreds of soldiers were deployed to assist with rescue operations as aftershocks continued to rumble through the region. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned of the possibility of more strong quakes over the coming week.

Mall Explosion Compounds the Disaster

The worst casualties came from the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, the prefecture's largest shopping center with around 200 stores. After the initial quake, an explosion — possibly caused by a ruptured gas line — tore away one side of the building, exposing steel beams and scattering debris across a vast parking lot.

Customers and employees had been evacuated immediately after the earthquake, according to mall operator Aeon, but workers remained inside. Between 20 and 30 employees were initially unaccounted for. By Wednesday morning, rescuers had pulled eight people from the rubble and confirmed that two women in their twenties had died. Ten people remained missing.

"The first strong jolt was followed by a strong horizontal shake — I felt as if we were in a washing machine. About 30 minutes later we heard a huge sound, as if huge trucks had collided."

— Atsushi Date, pharmacist near the Aeon Mall

Authorities are investigating a possible gas explosion as the cause of the blast, NTV reported.

Widespread Destruction Across Kumamoto

Beyond the mall, the earthquake caused extensive damage across the region. Aerial footage showed a section of a bridge collapsed into a river and highways with large fractures running through the pavement. In the town of Yatsushiro, columns of smoke rose from burning buildings, and at a Nippon Paper plant, a chimney tip fell, leaving two people in cardiac arrest and nine others missing.

Kumamoto Castle, a reconstruction of a historic fortress, suffered collapsed walls — echoing the damage from the devastating 2016 Kumamoto earthquakes that killed 273 people. A temple gate at Shokyoji Temple also collapsed.

One person died when a house collapsed during the earthquake, according to Kyodo News. A Vietnamese national working at a factory was also killed when a crane fell on him, the Vietnamese government confirmed — a reminder that foreign workers are among the most vulnerable in such disasters.

What Indians in Japan Should Know

Japan is home to a growing Indian community, estimated at over 46,000 as of 2025, concentrated in the Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya metropolitan areas. While Kyushu has a smaller Indian population, the region hosts manufacturing plants and IT operations that employ Indian workers.

The Indian Embassy in Tokyo has not issued a specific advisory for this earthquake but maintains an emergency helpline at +81-3-3262-2391. Indians in Japan who need consular assistance can also reach the embassy via its 24-hour emergency number.

More than 100 aftershocks have been detected since Tuesday's main quake, and the Meteorological Agency has warned residents to remain vigilant for landslides, particularly given the summer heat that poses additional heatstroke risks for evacuees and rescuers.
nri_angle: Thousands of Indians live and work in Japan, particularly in manufacturing and IT, and a Vietnamese factory worker was among the dead — raising concerns for all foreign workers in the affected region.
